faq.q: Can I work with Studio NOL in English?
faq.a: Yes — booking, quotes, mix notes, and revisions are all handled in English by email or KakaoTalk, and our remote mixing & mastering runs entirely in English. For an in-person session in Seoul, let us know your needs when you book and we'll set things up smoothly.

faq.q: Can I book remotely from outside Korea?
faq.a: Absolutely. Many international clients book via email or KakaoTalk before arriving in Seoul. We also offer online mixing and mastering — send us your recorded files and we handle the rest.
Final WAV and MP3 files are delivered via Google Drive or WeTransfer, typically within 3–7 business days after the session. Revisions are included in the package.

faq.q: What is included in a basic vocal session?
faq.a: A basic vocal session includes studio time with a professional engineer, Neumann microphone, treated recording booth, and a dry vocal WAV file. Mixing and mastering are available as add-ons.

faq.q: Do you offer online mixing-only service?
faq.a: Yes. Upload your recorded tracks and we handle mixing and mastering remotely. This is popular with artists who have their own home recording setup and want professional post-production.

faq.title: Practice Room FAQ
faq.subtitle: Frequently asked questions about the studio.

items.q: Which areas in Eunpyeong-gu are nearby?
items.a: We are located right next to Dongmyeong Girls' High School. It's a 5-minute walk from Yeonsinnae Station, making it highly accessible from Yeonsinnae, Bulgwang, Gusan, Yeokchon, and Eungam.

items.q: Is the practice room available 24 hours?
items.a: Yes. Resident members can access their rooms freely 24/7 via individual door lock codes.

items.q: How about parking and public transportation?
items.a: You can use the affordable public parking lot in Daejo-dong, a 1-2 minute walk away. Public transit access is easy via Bulgwang Station or Yeonsinnae Station (Lines 3 and 6), and the bus stop "Dongmyeong Girls' High School / Catholic Bulgwang-dong Church" is right in front.

items.q: Can I freely use heating and cooling in summer and winter?
items.a: Each room is equipped with the latest independent, draft-free HVAC system, providing comfort year-round.

items.q: Is it safe to leave instruments or gear?
items.a: Ten CCTV cameras record corridors and common areas 24/7, and each room has its own digital door lock for security.

items.q: How good is the soundproofing?
items.a: Our recording-studio-grade STC system delivers 60dB+ measured attenuation (STC 60+), nearly eliminating noise between rooms. Excellent immersion for vocals, voiceovers, and MIDI work.

items.q: How much does the practice room cost?
items.a: Monthly plans start from ₩360K (no deposit), the most reasonable price in Eunpyeong-gu. 50% off your first month with a 1-year+ contract. Includes 24/7 door-lock access, HVAC, and instrument storage.

items.q: What are the conditions for monthly music practice room residency?
items.a: No deposit required — prepaid monthly basis. Minimum contract is 1 month, with 24/7 individual door lock access, instrument/equipment storage, and individual HVAC control included. 50% off your first month is available with a 1-year+ contract.

items.q: Can I stay overnight at the practice room?
items.a: Yes — residents can stay for long sessions, show prep, or late-night recording. With individual door-lock access, HVAC, 24/7 private shower, and lobby amenities, overnight stays are comfortable. Details explained during the inquiry.

faqItems.question: How is an EP different from releasing multiple singles?
faqItems.answer: Multiple singles are each independent releases. An EP is one complete body of work. The curation work — track order, tone, and world-building across tracks — is only possible with an EP. If you want to build a solid fanbase, an EP leaves a stronger impression.

faqItems.question: Does cost go up proportionally with more tracks?
faqItems.answer: It varies by session lineup, track count, and arrangement scope — not a simple multiplier. We understand the full scope first, then give a custom quote. Tell us about the songs you have in the free consultation.

faqItems.question: Does an EP need a lead single?
faqItems.answer: It's not required. But a lead single is effective for building anticipation before the EP drops. We decide together based on your situation and timeline.

faqItems.question: Can we release an EP quickly?
faqItems.answer: Yes. If the songs and demos are ready and session scope is small, 3-4 months can work. If song selection, arrangement, session recording, and a lead-single campaign all need to be designed from scratch, 5-6 months or more is safer. We propose the timeline after reviewing your current situation.

faqItems.question: How long does a full album take?
faqItems.answer: For an 8-track album, if the songs and demos are ready, 6-8 months can be realistic. If song selection, arrangement, session recording, lead singles, and critics/media PR all need to be designed from scratch, 9-12 months is more realistic. We review song readiness and target release date first in consultation.

faqItems.question: Can you help with arts grants or crowdfunding?
faqItems.answer: We have experience with this. We can discuss arts council grants, regional arts funding, and crowdfunding directions in the consultation. Results, however, cannot be guaranteed.

faqItems.question: Can additional costs come up beyond the base rate?
faqItems.answer: Yes, varying by session lineup, track count, and arrangement scope. Cover artwork, music video, extra session musicians, physical release production, etc. are separate. We give a full custom quote after understanding the complete scope in consultation. No hidden costs.

faqItems.question: Can a full album get me on the charts?
faqItems.answer: We can't guarantee that. In the indie scene, a full album's value is in critical recognition and scene standing more than chart rankings. We work to open that path together.

faqItems.question: I've already released a first album. Can I still work with you?
faqItems.answer: Absolutely. A second album is about the narrative thread connecting it to the first and showing growth. We design the direction for a better second album by referencing your previous work.

items.question: What exactly is the release project?
items.answer: It's a project that walks with you through every step of releasing music — planning, recording, session musician coordination, mixing, mastering, distribution, and media PR. Vocal recording, mixing, and mastering are done in-house at Studio NOL, while instrumental sessions and critics/media connections run through the 15-year indie scene network. Single, EP, and full album each have their own pace and budget — check each page for the specific scope and how pricing is determined.

items.question: What if I change my mind or my schedule shifts mid-project?
items.answer: Because the project runs in stages, it's possible to pause or slow the pace midway. You only settle costs for the stages already completed and can take a break. Even if the song's direction shifts significantly, we discuss it again and find a path together — the refund policy is explained clearly during the free consultation.

items.question: I'm on a tight budget — can I commission only part of the process?
items.answer: Yes. We recommend the full release process, but you can also commission individual stages: vocal recording only / mixing only / mastering only. Partial quotes are based on our rate sheet (vocal recording ₩100K/hour, mixing from ₩200K, etc.). Note: media PR and distribution accompaniment are only included with full-process commissions.

items.question: I've already started recording elsewhere — can you join mid-process?
items.answer: Yes. We can receive tracks or stems recorded at another studio and continue with mixing, mastering, distribution, and PR. That said, we'll listen first and tell you honestly about any limitations caused by vocal tone or recording-environment differences.

items.question: What kind of artists have you worked with?
items.answer: Tierliner · The Projectors · Kang Ho-jung · Samgakjeonpasa · Namjae — 70+ releases with a wide range of indie artists: singer-songwriters, bands, jazz, experimental electronic music, and compilation projects. The discography section and portfolio page show a selection.

items.question: How does the free consultation work?
items.answer: Share your song and situation casually on KakaoTalk → 30-minute free consultation (video call or studio visit) → custom quote and timeline within 48 hours. You don't need to decide at the consultation. If it turns out not to be the right fit, we'll help you find another path.
